spec: Create a view named `evaluate` that finds the most critical city parks needing tree maintenance. You are given tables for parks, trees, and health assessments. Join these tables to calculate the total number of diseased trees per park. Filter the records to only include parks located in the northern district and where the tree age is greater than fifty years. Group the results by the park name and the assigned maintenance manager. Only include parks that have more than twenty diseased trees. Order the final list by the number of diseased trees in descending order.

title: Youth soccer league statistics
spec: Write a query named `rankings` that calculates the performance of youth soccer teams. Use the tables for teams, registered players, and match statistics. Join them together to find the total goals scored by players in the forward position. Filter the data to include only matches played in the autumn season and where the player attended at least ten practice sessions. Group the output by the team name and the head coach. Return only those teams with more than thirty goals in total. Sort the results from highest to lowest goal count.

title: Local bakery ingredient sourcing
spec: Create a procedure `sourcing()` that identifies reliable ingredient suppliers for a bakery chain. The database has tables for suppliers, ingredients, and delivery shipments. Link these tables to calculate the average delivery delay in days for each supplier. Restrict the data to organic ingredients and shipments that occurred in the last quarter. Group the information by the supplier name and their home city. Filter the aggregated results to only show suppliers with an average delay of less than two days. Sort the output alphabetically by the supplier name.

title: Amateur astronomy telescope usage
spec: Write a query `utilization` to find the most active amateur astronomy groups. You have tables storing observatories, registered users, and viewing sessions. Connect these tables to determine the total hours spent viewing deep sky objects. Filter the records to only include weekend sessions and users who have an advanced certification. Group the findings by the observatory name and the region it is located in. Keep only the observatories that logged over one hundred hours of viewing time. Order the final report by the total hours in descending order.

title: High school debate tournament
spec: Create a view `advancers` that lists the high schools qualifying for the state debate championship. The system contains tables for schools, debaters, and judge scores. Join these together to find the average score for each school. Apply filters to only include senior debaters and debates that were in the policy category. Group the results by the school name and the school district. Retain only the schools that achieved an average score above eighty five points. Sort the qualifying schools by their average score from highest to lowest.

title: Volunteer river cleanup drives
spec: Write a procedure `impact()` that summarizes the trash collected during river cleanup campaigns. You have tables for river locations, cleanup events, and volunteer participations. Link the tables to calculate the total weight of trash collected per river. Limit the data to events held in the spring and volunteers who are local residents. Group the output by the river name and the state it flows through. Only display rivers where the total collected trash exceeds five hundred pounds. Order the list by the total weight descending.

title: Independent bookshop rare editions
spec: Create a query `valuations` that identifies bookshops holding highly valuable rare books. The database includes tables for bookshops, book inventory, and expert appraisals. Join the tables to calculate the total appraised value of first edition books at each shop. Filter the dataset to include only hardcover books and appraisals completed this year. Group the records by the shop name and the city it operates in. Show only the shops whose total rare book value is greater than ten thousand dollars. Sort the results alphabetically by the city.

title: Regional choir competition
spec: Write a view `finalists` that selects the top performing choirs in a regional music festival. Use tables for choirs, choir members, and performance scores. Connect the data to find the average harmony score for each choir. Filter the entries to include only adult choirs and performances in the classical category. Group the information by the choir name and their conductor. Retain only the choirs that scored above ninety points on average. Order the final output by the score descending.

title: Mountain bike trail maintenance
spec: Create a procedure `hazards()` that highlights mountain bike trails needing urgent repairs. You are provided with tables for trails, trail segments, and logged repair requests. Join them to count the total number of severe hazard reports per trail. Restrict the data to downhill segments and reports filed in the last month. Group the results by the trail name and the park ranger assigned to it. Filter the groups to only include trails with more than five severe reports. Sort the list from the most reports to the least.

title: Urban community gardens
spec: Write a query `yields` that calculates the most productive community gardens. The system has tables for gardens, individual plots, and harvest records. Link these tables to sum the total pounds of vegetables harvested. Filter the records to only include summer harvests and plots managed by community groups. Group the data by the garden name and the neighborhood. Include only gardens that produced over two thousand pounds of food. Order the results by the total harvest weight in descending order.

title: Amateur pottery classes
spec: Create a view `popularity` that finds the most successful pottery instructors. You have tables for studios, instructors, and class enrollments. Join the tables to determine the total number of students taught by each instructor. Filter the data to include only wheel throwing classes and instructors with more than five years of experience. Group the findings by the instructor name and the studio they work at. Keep only those instructors who have taught over two hundred students. Sort the output by the total student count descending.

title: Classic car show entries
spec: Write a procedure `winners()` that identifies the classic car clubs with the most award winning vehicles. The database contains tables for car clubs, registered vehicles, and show awards. Connect these tables to count the total number of gold ribbons won by each club. Limit the data to vehicles manufactured before nineteen seventy and awards from national level shows. Group the results by the club name and the state they are based in. Show only clubs that have won at least ten gold ribbons. Order the list alphabetically by the club name.

title: Local chess club tournaments
spec: Create a query `standings` that lists the top performing chess clubs in a statewide league. Use tables for regions, chess clubs, and match results. Join them to calculate the total number of matches won by each club. Filter the records to include only standard time control matches and clubs that have active memberships. Group the output by the club name and their region. Retain only the clubs that have won more than fifty matches this season. Sort the final standings by the number of wins from highest to lowest.

title: Film student short movies
spec: Write a view `selections` that highlights universities producing successful short films. You are given tables for universities, student directors, and festival submissions. Link the tables to count the total number of awards won by films from each university. Restrict the data to documentary films and directors in their senior year. Group the information by the university name and the country it is located in. Only include universities with more than three documentary awards. Order the results by the award count descending.

title: Regional spelling bee
spec: Create a procedure `qualifiers()` that finds the school districts with the strongest spelling bee contestants. The database has tables for districts, schools, and contestant scores. Join the tables to calculate the average vocabulary score for each district. Filter the dataset to include only middle school contestants and scores from the regional finals. Group the records by the district name and the state. Show only the districts where the average score is above ninety five. Sort the output from highest to lowest average score.

title: City marathon training groups
spec: Write a query `endurance` that identifies the most active marathon training clubs. You have tables for city zones, training clubs, and runner mileage logs. Connect these tables to sum the total miles run by each club. Limit the data to weekend long runs and runners preparing for a full marathon. Group the results by the club name and their home zone. Keep only the clubs that have logged a combined total of over ten thousand miles. Order the final list by the total miles in descending order.

title: Historic house museum tours
spec: Create a view `attendance` that lists historic houses with the highest visitor turnout. The system contains tables for counties, historic houses, and daily visitor logs. Join the tables to calculate the total number of visitors for each house. Filter the entries to only include guided tours and houses built before the nineteenth century. Group the data by the house name and the county it resides in. Retain only houses that received over five thousand visitors this year. Sort the output by the visitor count descending.

title: Amateur baking competitions
spec: Write a procedure `excellence()` that highlights the most consistent amateur bakers. Use tables for competition categories, registered bakers, and judge evaluations. Link the tables to find the average presentation score for each baker. Filter the data to include only pastry categories and bakers who have entered at least three competitions. Group the findings by the baker name and their home town. Show only the bakers who maintain an average presentation score above eight out of ten. Order the list by the average score from highest to lowest.

title: Toll Road Revenue Analysis
spec: Implement `summarize(records)` to analyze toll road booth collections. The database has a registered vehicles table and a toll transactions table. Join them by matching the vehicle registration to the plate number. Filter to include only east plaza transactions where the fee is greater than four. Group by vehicle type, select it, and sum the fees as total revenue, ordering the results by this total in descending order. For example, a sedan with east plaza fees of five and six outputs sedan with total revenue eleven.

title: Lumber Mill Timber Processing
spec: Implement `analyze(logs)` to calculate timber processing volumes at a lumber mill. The database features a tree species table and a processed logs table. Join them by matching the tree identifier to the origin tree. Filter to keep only morning shift logs where the length is greater than ten feet. Group by species name, select it, and sum the volumes as total volume, ordering by total volume in descending order. For example, oak logs of twenty and thirty cubic feet yield oak with total volume fifty.

title: Archery Tournament Scores
spec: Implement `report(scores)` to tabulate archery tournament scores. The database holds a competing archers table and a target rounds table. Join them by matching the competitor number to the player identifier. Filter for final stage rounds where the wind speed was less than five. Group by archer division, select the division, and calculate the average score as average precision, ordering by this average descending. For example, a junior division archer scoring nine and ten results in junior with average precision nine point five.

title: Bridge Structural Inspections
spec: Implement `summarize(reports)` to assess bridge structural safety. The database stores a bridges table and an inspection reports table. Join them by matching the structure code to the target bridge. Filter to include only bridges built before two thousand where the safety score is below seventy. Group by material type, select it, and count the reports as flag count, ordering by flag count descending. For example, three failing reports for steel bridges output steel with a flag count of three.

title: Billiard Tournament Matches
spec: Implement `analyze(matches)` to evaluate billiard tournament performance. The system contains a registered players table and a match results table. Join them by matching the registration number to the contestant identifier. Filter to include only eight ball matches where the duration exceeded thirty minutes. Group by player skill tier, select the tier, and sum the pocketed balls as total balls, ordering by total balls descending. For example, an amateur tier player pocketing seven and eight balls yields amateur with total balls fifteen.

title: Mining Excavation Tonnage
spec: Implement `report(yields)` to track mining excavation tonnage. The database includes a mining sites table and an excavation logs table. Join them by matching the plot number to the source plot. Filter for diamond extraction where the rock volume is greater than twenty tons. Group by mineral grade, select it, and sum the volumes as total volume, ordering by total volume descending. For example, high grade diamond extractions of twenty five and thirty tons output high grade with total volume fifty five.

title: Ferry Terminal Boarding
spec: Implement `summarize(entries)` to monitor ferry terminal passenger boarding. The database features a ferry docks table and a passenger boarding logs table. Join them by matching the facility code to the location code. Filter to include only morning rush hour departures where the passenger count is greater than one hundred. Group by ferry vessel name, select the name, and sum the passengers as total passengers, ordering descending by this total. For example, the seabreeze vessel boarding two hundred and three hundred passengers yields seabreeze with total passengers five hundred.

title: Knitting Pattern Yarn Requirements
spec: Implement `analyze(patterns)` to review knitting pattern yarn usage. The system holds a knitting patterns table and a yarn materials table. Join them by matching the design number to the target design. Filter for intermediate difficulty patterns where the yarn weight is worsted. Group by garment category, select the category, and average the yardage needed as average yardage, ordering by the average descending. For example, worsted sweater patterns requiring eight hundred and one thousand yards output sweater with average yardage nine hundred.

title: Sumo Wrestling Tournaments
spec: Implement `report(bouts)` to review sumo wrestling tournament bouts. The database stores a wrestlers table and a match results table. Join them by matching the athlete number to the fighter identifier. Filter to include only top division bouts where the match duration exceeded two minutes. Group by winning technique, select it, and count the victories as total wins, ordering by total wins descending. For example, two lengthy top division bouts won by a push out result in push out with total wins two.

title: Elevator Maintenance Logs
spec: Implement `summarize(faults)` to track elevator maintenance activity. The database contains commercial buildings and elevator fault logs tables. Join them by matching the property code to the site code. Filter for mechanical faults where the downtime exceeded four hours. Group by building zoning type, select it, and count the faults as total faults, ordering by total faults descending. For example, two mechanical faults in commercial zones yield commercial with total faults two.

title: Leatherworking Crafts
spec: Implement `analyze(crafts)` to audit leatherworking workshop production. The system includes a leather hides table and a crafted items table. Join them by matching the batch number to the material batch. Filter for hand stitched items where the production time is greater than five hours. Group by item category, select it, and sum the hours spent as total labor, ordering descending by total labor. For example, two hand stitched satchels taking six and seven hours output satchel with total labor thirteen.

title: Paintball Arena Matches
spec: Implement `report(games)` to evaluate paintball arena usage. The database features playing fields and completed matches tables. Join them by matching the zone code to the arena code. Filter for capture the flag modes where paint fired exceeds five thousand rounds. Group by field layout type, select it, and count the matches as match count, ordering by match count descending. For example, three heavy usage matches on an urban layout yield urban with match count three.

title: Ice Hockey Penalty Minutes
spec: Implement `summarize(penalties)` to summarize ice hockey penalty minutes. The database holds hockey players and penalty infractions tables. Join them by matching the roster number to the offender number. Filter for major penalties where the duration is exactly five minutes. Group by player position, select it, and sum the penalty minutes as total minutes, ordering descending by total minutes. For example, a defenseman getting two five minute majors outputs defenseman with total minutes ten.

title: Forklift Battery Recharges
spec: Implement `analyze(cycles)` to monitor forklift battery efficiency. The system stores warehouse forklifts and battery charge cycles tables. Join them by matching the equipment code to the machine code. Filter for fast charging sessions where the ending voltage is above forty eight volts. Group by forklift manufacturer, select it, and average the charge duration as average time, ordering by average time descending. For example, charging a toyota forklift for forty and fifty minutes yields toyota with average time forty five.

title: Parade Float Inspections
spec: Implement `report(inspections)` to review parade float safety inspections. The database contains parade organizations and float inspection logs tables. Join them by matching the sponsor code to the builder code. Filter for night parades where the float weight exceeds two tons. Group by float theme, select it, and count the violations as total violations, ordering descending by total violations. For example, finding three violations on heavy night time floral floats outputs floral with total violations three.

title: Printing Press Ink Consumption
spec: Implement `summarize(jobs)` to calculate printing press ink consumption. The database includes printing presses and print jobs tables. Join them by matching the hardware number to the machine number. Filter for glossy magazine jobs where the page count is greater than one thousand. Group by ink color, select it, and sum the ink used as total ink, ordering by total ink descending. For example, two large print jobs using fifty and sixty liters of cyan yield cyan with total ink one hundred ten.

title: Carpet Cleaning Service Appointments
spec: Implement `analyze(visits)` to audit carpet cleaning service appointments. The system features cleaning technicians and service visits tables. Join them by matching the badge number to the worker badge. Filter for deep cleaning services where the area cleaned is larger than five hundred square feet. Group by technician certification level, select it, and sum the area cleaned as total area, ordering descending by total area. For example, an expert technician cleaning six hundred and eight hundred square feet outputs expert with total area fourteen hundred.

title: Curling Rink Sheet Pebbling
spec: Implement `report(logs)` to evaluate curling rink ice maintenance. The database holds ice sheets and pebbling logs tables. Join them by matching the lane code to the target lane. Filter for tournament preparations where the water temperature is below fifty degrees. Group by sheet location, select it, and count the pebbling runs as total runs, ordering by total runs descending. For example, five tournament pebbling runs on the center sheet yield center with total runs five.

title: Marching Band Uniform Inventory
spec: Implement `summarize(items)` to track marching band uniform assignments. The database stores band members and uniform items tables. Join them by matching the enrollment number to the student number. Filter for brass section members where the uniform condition is marked as poor. Group by uniform size, select it, and count the items as replacement count, ordering by replacement count descending. For example, finding four poor condition large uniforms outputs large with replacement count four.

title: Helicopter Sightseeing Tours
spec: Implement `analyze(flights)` to analyze helicopter sightseeing tours. The system contains tour helicopters and flight logs tables. Join them by matching the tail number to the aircraft number. Filter for sunset tours where the passenger count is at least four. Group by flight route name, select it, and sum the flight minutes as total duration, ordering descending by total duration. For example, two sunset canyon tours lasting forty and fifty minutes yield canyon with total duration ninety.

title: Sewing Machine Needle Replacements
spec: Implement `report(wear)` to monitor sewing machine needle wear. The database features sewing machines and needle replacement logs tables. Join them by matching the serial number to the unit number. Filter for denim stitching tasks where the machine speed was set above high. Group by needle brand, select it, and count the breakages as total breakages, ordering by total breakages descending. For example, three high speed denim breakages for a singer needle output singer with total breakages three.

title: Scaffolding Rental Periods
spec: Implement `summarize(rentals)` to evaluate scaffolding rental periods. The database includes construction sites and scaffolding rentals tables. Join them by matching the project code to the destination code. Filter for exterior painting projects where the rental duration exceeds thirty days. Group by scaffolding material type, select it, and sum the rental fees as total revenue, ordering descending by total revenue. For example, steel scaffolding rented for forty days twice at five hundred dollars each yields steel with total revenue one thousand.

title: Tattoo Parlor Ink Mixing
spec: Implement `analyze(sessions)` to audit tattoo parlor ink mixing sessions. The system holds tattoo artists and ink mixing logs tables. Join them by matching the license number to the creator number. Filter for custom color requests where the volume mixed is greater than two ounces. Group by base pigment color, select it, and sum the volumes as total volume, ordering by total volume descending. For example, mixing three and four ounces of custom crimson ink outputs crimson with total volume seven.

title: Swimming Pool Chlorine Levels
spec: Implement `report(levels)` to track swimming pool chlorine applications. The database stores public pools and chemical logs tables. Join them by matching the facility number to the basin number. Filter for outdoor pools where the measured acid level was below seven. Group by chlorine brand, select it, and sum the dosage applied as total dosage, ordering by total dosage descending. For example, adding two and three gallons of clearwater chlorine to outdoor pools yields clearwater with total dosage five.

title: Ice Skating Rink Zamboni Runs
spec: Implement `summarize(sessions)` to review ice skating rink zamboni operations. The database contains rink schedules and resurfacing logs tables. Join them by matching the block code to the time block. Filter for public skating sessions where the water volume used was over one hundred gallons. Group by zamboni driver name, select it, and count the resurfacing runs as total runs, ordering descending by total runs. For example, driver john completing two heavy water runs yields john with total runs two.

title: University scholarship eligibility
spec: Create a view that calculates each student's total credits and average grade across all courses. The database has three tables: students with identifier, full name, and major program; courses with identifier, credit value, and department name; and enrollments linking student identifier to course identifier along with a numeric grade. After creating the summary view, write a query that selects the full name, total credits, and average grade of students who major in engineering and have an average grade above eighty five, specifically including only those who have completed at least one course in the physics department. The final result should sort candidates by their average grade from highest to lowest, followed by their total credits from highest to lowest. Example input: a student named Alice in engineering with ninety in a physics course and ninety in a math course. Example output: Alice, six credits, ninety average. Use the entry point `evaluate(database)`.

title: Car rental agency fleet utilization
spec: Write a script `utilization(database)` that analyzes rental patterns across three tables: vehicles with identifier, make, model, and purchase year; branches with branch identifier, city, and capacity; and rentals linking vehicle and branch identifiers with start date, end date, and total revenue. First, create a view that calculates the total revenue and total days rented for each vehicle. Then, write a query that retrieves the branch city, vehicle make, and total revenue for vehicles purchased after two thousand eighteen that generated more than five thousand in revenue and were rented for over thirty days. Sort the final output alphabetically by branch city, then by total revenue from highest to lowest. Example input: a branch in Chicago, a Ford vehicle purchased in two thousand nineteen, rented for forty days generating six thousand. Example output: Chicago, Ford, six thousand.

title: Online marketplace vendor payouts
spec: Use `payouts(database)` to generate a commission report. The system has vendors with identifier, business name, and account status, alongside a sales table recording sale identifier, vendor identifier, sale amount, and transaction date. A commission table maintains vendor identifier, percentage rate, and active flag. First create a view that computes the total sales amount for each vendor in the current year. Then write a query linking vendors, their active commission rate, and their total sales to select the business name, total sales, and calculated commission amount for vendors whose account status is active and total sales exceed ten thousand. Order the results by the commission amount from highest to lowest, then by business name. Example input: vendor Zenith active with ten percent commission, total sales twelve thousand. Example output: Zenith, twelve thousand, twelve hundred.

title: Tech conference workshop attendance
spec: Implement `attendance(database)` to identify popular conference sessions. The schema includes attendees with identifier, full name, and ticket type, workshops with identifier, title, and maximum capacity, and registrations linking attendee and workshop identifiers with registration timestamp and waitlist status. Create a view that counts the number of confirmed attendees and waitlisted attendees for each workshop. Write a query that finds workshops where the confirmed count equals the maximum capacity and the waitlist has more than ten people. Return the workshop title, maximum capacity, and waitlist count, sorting the output by waitlist count descending, then workshop title ascending. Example input: workshop Advanced AI with capacity fifty, fifty confirmed, fifteen waitlisted. Example output: Advanced AI, fifty, fifteen.

title: Hospital surgical ward efficiency
spec: Create a reporting script `efficiency(database)` for surgical outcomes. The medical database has surgeons with identifier, full name, and specialty, surgeries with identifier, surgeon identifier, procedure name, and duration in minutes, and outcomes linking surgery identifier to patient recovery days and complication flag. Build a view that averages the duration and recovery days for each surgeon. Write a subsequent query that joins surgeons, their average metrics, and counts of surgeries with complications. Select the surgeon full name, specialty, average duration, and total complications for those specializing in cardiology who have an average duration under one hundred twenty minutes and fewer than three total complications. Sort by total complications ascending, then average duration ascending. Example input: surgeon Bob in cardiology, average duration ninety minutes, one complication. Example output: Bob, cardiology, ninety, one.

title: Real estate agent commission ranking
spec: Develop `ranking(database)` to evaluate top real estate agents. The property database contains agents with identifier, full name, and office location, properties with identifier, agent identifier, listing price, and sale price, and transactions recording property identifier, closing date, and buyer name. Form a view that aggregates total sales volume and count of properties sold for each agent. Write a query that retrieves the agent full name, office location, total sales volume, and average sale to list price ratio for agents in the downtown office who have sold more than five properties and achieved a total volume over two million. Order the final report by total sales volume descending. Example input: downtown agent Clara, six properties sold, three million volume, ninety eight percent ratio. Example output: Clara, downtown, three million, ninety eight percent.

title: Gym membership retention
spec: Write `retention(database)` to analyze gym member activity. The fitness database includes members with identifier, full name, and join date, classes with identifier, class name, and instructor name, and attendance logs recording member identifier, class identifier, date, and completed status. First set up a view that counts the total classes attended and distinct months visited for each member. Then query the database to find members who joined before two thousand twenty, attended more than fifty classes, and visited in at least ten distinct months. Return the member full name, join date, and total classes attended, sorting the results by total classes attended descending, then full name. Example input: member David joined two thousand nineteen, sixty classes, twelve months. Example output: David, two thousand nineteen, sixty.

title: Restaurant supply chain sourcing
spec: Use `sourcing(database)` to audit ingredient suppliers. The restaurant system holds suppliers with identifier, company name, and region, ingredients with identifier, ingredient name, and category, and deliveries recording delivery identifier, supplier identifier, ingredient identifier, quantity delivered, and rejection reason. Create a summary view that calculates the total quantity delivered and the count of rejected deliveries per supplier. Write a query to find suppliers in the northwest region providing dairy ingredients who delivered over one thousand units but have more than five rejected deliveries. Select the company name, ingredient name, total quantity, and rejection count, sorting by rejection count descending, then company name. Example input: supplier FreshFarm in northwest, dairy ingredient milk, two thousand delivered, six rejections. Example output: FreshFarm, milk, two thousand, six.

title: Software company bug bounty rewards
spec: Implement `bounties(database)` to calculate hacker payouts. The security database contains hackers with identifier, handle, and country, bugs with identifier, hacker identifier, severity level, and resolution status, and payouts linking bug identifier to monetary reward and payment date. Construct a view that totals the monetary rewards and counts the high severity bugs for each hacker. Create a query that joins hackers and the summary view to extract the handle, country, total reward, and high severity count for hackers from either the United States or Canada who have at least three high severity bugs and a total reward exceeding five thousand. Order by total reward descending and handle alphabetically. Example input: hacker cyber ninja from Canada, four high severity bugs, six thousand reward. Example output: cyber ninja, Canada, six thousand, four.

title: Online academy graduation metrics
spec: Write `graduations(database)` to track student progress. The learning system features students with identifier, full name, and enrollment date, modules with identifier, course name, and required passing score, and assessments recording student identifier, module identifier, attempt date, and achieved score. Build a view that finds the highest score each student achieved for each module. Write a query that selects the student full name, course name, and highest score for students who enrolled in the current year and achieved a score greater than or equal to the required passing score on their first or second attempt. Order the output by course name ascending, then highest score descending. Example input: student Emma enrolled this year, course Python, required eighty, achieved ninety. Example output: Emma, Python, ninety.

title: Maritime cargo port congestion
spec: Develop `congestion(database)` to monitor shipping delays. The maritime database has ships with identifier, vessel name, and home port, containers with identifier, ship identifier, destination port, and weight, and voyages recording ship identifier, departure date, expected arrival date, and actual arrival date. Set up a view that calculates the total container weight and average delay in days for each ship. Write a final query retrieving the vessel name, home port, total weight, and average delay for ships bound for international ports that have an average delay greater than two days and carry more than ten thousand tons. Sort by average delay descending, then vessel name. Example input: ship Oceanic from Seattle, twenty thousand tons, three days delay. Example output: Oceanic, Seattle, twenty thousand, three.

title: Cinema loyalty program points
spec: Use `loyalty(database)` to reward frequent moviegoers. The theater database includes customers with identifier, full name, and tier status, screenings with identifier, movie title, and genre, and tickets linking customer identifier to screening identifier with purchase date and ticket price. Create a view that computes the total amount spent and the number of distinct movies watched by each customer. Query the database to retrieve the customer full name, tier status, total spent, and movie count for customers in the gold tier who have watched at least five distinct movies and spent over one hundred. Order the results by total spent descending, then full name ascending. Example input: customer Frank in gold tier, watched six movies, spent one hundred twenty. Example output: Frank, gold, one hundred twenty, six.

title: Veterinary clinic vaccination schedules
spec: Write `vaccinations(database)` to identify overdue pets. The clinic database contains pets with identifier, pet name, and species, vaccines with identifier, vaccine name, and validity months, and records tracking pet identifier, vaccine identifier, administration date, and veterinarian name. Build a view that determines the expiration date of the most recent administration for each pet and vaccine combination. Write a query that lists the pet name, species, vaccine name, and expiration date for dogs or cats whose vaccination expired within the last thirty days or will expire in the next fourteen days. Sort by expiration date ascending, then pet name. Example input: dog Rex, rabies vaccine, expired ten days ago. Example output: Rex, dog, rabies, ten days ago.

title: Hotel chain customer reviews
spec: Implement `reviews(database)` to evaluate hotel performance. The hospitality database features hotels with identifier, property name, and star rating, stays with identifier, hotel identifier, guest name, and checkout date, and ratings linking stay identifier to numeric score and text comment. Construct a view that calculates the average numeric score and total number of ratings for each hotel. Create a query that retrieves the property name, star rating, average score, and total ratings for five star hotels that have an average score below four and more than fifty total ratings. Order the output by average score ascending, then total ratings descending. Example input: hotel Grand Plaza, five stars, average score three point eight, sixty ratings. Example output: Grand Plaza, five stars, three point eight, sixty.

title: Airline frequent flyer tiers
spec: Use `tiers(database)` to update passenger statuses. The flight database includes passengers with identifier, full name, and current tier, flights with identifier, origin, destination, and distance, and boarding passes linking passenger identifier, flight identifier, flight date, and class multiplier. Create a view that calculates the total qualifying miles for each passenger by multiplying flight distance by the class multiplier for flights taken this year. Write a query selecting the passenger full name, current tier, and total qualifying miles for passengers who accumulated more than fifty thousand miles but are currently in the silver tier. Sort the results by total miles descending. Example input: passenger George, silver tier, sixty thousand miles. Example output: George, silver, sixty thousand.

title: Mobile game player spending tiers
spec: Develop `spending(database)` to classify high value players. The gaming database has players with identifier, username, and region, items with identifier, item name, and category, and purchases recording player identifier, item identifier, purchase date, and cost. Set up a view that totals the cost of all purchases and counts the distinct items bought by each player. Query the database to find players in the European region who spent over five hundred and bought at least twenty distinct items, returning the username, region, total spent, and distinct item count. Order by total spent descending, then username ascending. Example input: player Hero in Europe, spent six hundred, twenty five items. Example output: Hero, Europe, six hundred, twenty five.

title: Local library branch performance
spec: Write `performance(database)` to analyze book circulation. The library database contains branches with identifier, branch name, and district, books with identifier, title, and genre, and checkouts linking book identifier, branch identifier, checkout date, and return date. Create a view that computes the total checkouts and average loan duration in days for each branch. Write a query that selects the branch name, district, total checkouts, and average loan duration for branches in the central district that have over five thousand checkouts and an average loan duration of less than fourteen days. Sort the output by total checkouts descending. Example input: Main branch in central district, six thousand checkouts, ten days average. Example output: Main, central, six thousand, ten.

title: Courier fleet performance bonuses
spec: Implement `rewards(database)` to calculate driver bonuses. The delivery database includes drivers with identifier, full name, and vehicle type, routes with identifier, zone, and base pay, and deliveries recording driver identifier, route identifier, delivery date, and on time status. Build a view that counts the total deliveries and the number of on time deliveries for each driver. Write a query returning the full name, vehicle type, total deliveries, and on time percentage for drivers using electric vans who completed at least one hundred deliveries with an on time percentage above ninety five. Order the results by on time percentage descending, then full name. Example input: driver Helen, electric van, one hundred twenty deliveries, ninety eight percent on time. Example output: Helen, electric van, one hundred twenty, ninety eight percent.

title: Moon Base Power Consumption
spec: Write a SQL function `evaluate(limit)` that calculates total power usage across lunar base sectors. The database has a table for sectors with their sector identifier and primary function, and a table for power logs recording the sector identifier, date, and kilowatts used. The function should calculate the sum of kilowatts used per sector function, excluding logs where kilowatts are below the limit. Combine the tables using the sector identifier, group the results by the primary function, and return the function and total kilowatts. Order the final results from highest to lowest total kilowatts. Example input: limit 50. Example output: (habitation, 4500), (research, 3200).

title: Medieval Tournament Jousting Scores
spec: Write a SQL procedure `rank(minimum)` that finds the top knights in a jousting tournament. The database contains a table for knights with their identifier and home region, and a table for matches containing the knight identifier, opponent identifier, and points scored. Calculate the total points for each knight and return their home region and total score. Only include knights who have scored more than the minimum points in a single match and whose total score across all matches exceeds one hundred. Combine the knights and matches tables, group by the knight identifier and region, and sort the results by total score descending. Example input: minimum 10. Example output: (wessex, 150), (northumbria, 120).

title: Galactic Federation Tax Evasion
spec: Write a SQL function `audit(year)` that identifies planetary systems underpaying federation taxes. You are provided a table of planets containing the planet identifier, system name, and population, and a table of tax payments containing the planet identifier, payment year, and credits paid. Calculate the required tax as population multiplied by ten, and find systems where the total credits paid in the given year is less than half the total required tax. Link the planets and tax payments, filter by the specified year, group by the system name, and return the system name along with the shortfall amount. Sort the output alphabetically by system name. Example input: year 3045. Example output: (andromeda, 500000), (orion, 120000).

title: Subterranean Drill Maintenance
spec: Develop a SQL function `schedule(depth)` that prioritizes maintenance for deep earth drilling rigs. There is a table of drills with their identifier, model name, and installation date, and a table of drill operations logging the drill identifier, depth reached, and vibration level. Find drills where the depth reached is greater than the provided depth and the vibration level exceeds eighty. Join the drills and operations tables, grouping by model name to find the maximum vibration level for each model. Return the model name and maximum vibration, filtering out any models where the installation date was before the year two thousand. Sort the results with the highest vibration first. Example input: depth 5000. Example output: (magma piercer, 95), (crust breaker, 88).

title: Mars Colony Food Rations
spec: Create a SQL function `ration(calories)` that identifies colonists needing dietary supplements. The database has a table of colonists with their identifier, name, and role, and a table of meal logs containing the colonist identifier, meal date, and calories consumed. Calculate the average daily calories for each colonist, considering only meals consumed in the last thirty days. Join the tables, group by the colonist name and role, and select those whose average is strictly below the target calories provided as input. Return the colonist name, role, and their average calories, ordering the list from lowest average to highest. Example input: calories 2000. Example output: (johnson, botanist, 1850), (smith, engineer, 1920).

title: Cybernetic Implant Failures
spec: Write a SQL procedure `investigate(threshold)` that finds manufacturers of faulty neural implants. A table of implants holds the implant identifier, manufacturer name, and batch number, while a table of patient reports records the implant identifier, report date, and severity score. Match the implants with their reports and compute the average severity score for each manufacturer. Only include reports where the severity score is greater than five. Group the data by manufacturer name and batch number, keeping only those groups where the average severity is above the given threshold and the count of reports is at least ten. Output the manufacturer name, batch number, and average severity, sorted by severity descending. Example input: threshold 7. Example output: (neural tech, batch forty, 8.5).

title: Deep Sea Trench Creatures
spec: Create a SQL function `catalog(pressure)` that analyzes species sightings in high pressure ocean zones. There is a table of submarines with their identifier, vessel name, and maximum depth, and a table of sightings recording the submarine identifier, species name, and water pressure at the time of sighting. Connect the submarines and sightings tables to find species spotted at a water pressure higher than the given pressure parameter. Group the records by species name and vessel name to count the total sightings for each pair. Return the species name, vessel name, and sighting count, excluding any counts less than three. Order the results alphabetically by species name. Example input: pressure 500. Example output: (giant squid, nautilus, 5), (anglerfish, sea explorer, 3).

title: Wizard Guild Potion Ingredients
spec: Implement a SQL procedure `restock(minimum)` that identifies rare potion ingredients running low across alchemist shops. A table of ingredients stores the identifier, ingredient name, and magical property, while a table of inventories holds the shop identifier, ingredient identifier, and quantity in stock. Combine the ingredients and inventories tables to sum the total quantity of each ingredient across all shops. Filter out any ingredients whose magical property is healing or protection. Group by the ingredient name and select only those where the total quantity is below the provided minimum. Return the ingredient name and total quantity, ordering by quantity ascending. Example input: minimum 50. Example output: (dragon scales, 12), (mandrake root, 34).

title: Time Travel Paradox Anomalies
spec: Write a SQL function `detect(variance)` that finds timeline disruptions caused by unauthorized chronal jumps. The database contains a table of agents with their identifier and clearance level, and a table of chronal jumps holding the agent identifier, destination year, and temporal variance score. Join the tables and calculate the total temporal variance caused by each agent. Filter the jumps to only include destination years prior to the year nineteen hundred. Group the results by the agent identifier and clearance level, and return the clearance level alongside the total variance if it exceeds the provided variance limit. Sort the output by total variance from highest to lowest. Example input: variance 100. Example output: (alpha, 350), (beta, 120).

title: Intergalactic Cargo Smuggling
spec: Create a SQL function `scan(weight)` that flags suspicious freight ships based on declared cargo. You have a table of ships with their identifier, registry port, and captain name, and a table of manifests with the ship identifier, cargo type, and tonnage. Join the ships and manifests to calculate the total tonnage of hazardous cargo types per ship. Only consider cargo types categorized as weapons or explosives, and ignore manifests where the tonnage is below the given weight limit. Group by the registry port and captain name, returning the registry port, captain name, and total tonnage. Order the results primarily by registry port alphabetically and secondarily by tonnage descending. Example input: weight 50. Example output: (omega station, zarkov, 500).

title: Steampunk Airship Racing
spec: Develop a SQL function `leaderboard(duration)` that ranks airship performance in a transcontinental race. A table of airships contains the identifier, vessel name, and engine type, while a table of race legs records the airship identifier, leg distance, and time taken. Link the tables and compute the average speed for each airship by dividing total distance by total time taken. Exclude any race legs where the time taken is greater than the duration parameter. Group the data by vessel name and engine type, and select airships that have completed at least five race legs. Return the vessel name, engine type, and average speed, sorted by average speed descending. Example input: duration 120. Example output: (cloud piercer, steam, 85), (wind rider, aether, 82).

title: Goblin Mine Gold Extraction
spec: Write a SQL procedure `yields(purity)` that evaluates the most productive goblin mining crews. The database has a table of crews with their identifier, clan name, and foreman, and a table of excavations with the crew identifier, ounces extracted, and gold purity percentage. Join the crews and excavations tables to find the total ounces extracted by each clan. Only include excavations where the gold purity percentage is greater than the provided purity limit. Group the results by clan name and foreman, filtering out clans that extracted less than one thousand ounces in total. Output the clan name, foreman, and total ounces, ordering by total ounces descending. Example input: purity 85. Example output: (iron tooth, grash, 1500).

title: Quantum Computer Qubit Stability
spec: Create a SQL function `calibrate(errors)` that identifies unstable quantum processors requiring recalibration. A processors table holds the identifier, architecture type, and location, and a stability log table records the processor identifier, test date, and error count. Match processors with their stability logs and find the maximum error count for each architecture type over the past week. Exclude processors located in the backup facility. Group by architecture type and location, and only return those where the maximum error count exceeds the errors parameter. Output the architecture type, location, and maximum error count, sorted from highest to lowest error count. Example input: errors 20. Example output: (topological, main lab, 45).

title: Superhero City Damage Claims
spec: Implement a SQL function `compensate(cost)` that summarizes property damage caused by hero interventions. A table of incidents contains the identifier, hero name, and city district, and a table of damage claims holds the incident identifier, property type, and repair cost. Join the tables to sum the repair costs for each hero across different city districts. Ignore claims for public roads and parks. Group by the hero name and city district, and select combinations where the total repair cost is higher than the given cost parameter. Output the hero name, city district, and total repair cost, ordering alphabetically by district and then descending by cost. Example input: cost 100000. Example output: (titan, downtown, 500000).

title: Cyborg Gladiator Arena
spec: Write a SQL function `rankings(wins)` that determines the most successful combat chassis models in the arena. There is a table of gladiators with their identifier, chassis model, and sponsor, and a table of matches logging the gladiator identifier, match duration, and outcome. Connect the gladiators and matches to count the total number of victory outcomes for each chassis model. Exclude matches that lasted longer than thirty minutes. Group the data by chassis model and sponsor, returning the chassis model, sponsor, and victory count for those with a victory count greater than the wins parameter. Sort the output by victory count descending. Example input: wins 15. Example output: (berserker, mega corp, 22).

title: Alien Flora Terraforming
spec: Develop a SQL procedure `monitor(acidity)` that tracks the growth of genetically modified plants on newly terraformed worlds. A table of planets contains the identifier, sector name, and surface temperature, while a table of plant samples records the planet identifier, species name, and soil acidity. Join the tables and count the distinct species names found in each sector. Only include samples where the soil acidity is lower than the acidity parameter and the surface temperature is above zero. Group by sector name and return the sector name alongside the distinct species count. Order the results by the species count from highest to lowest. Example input: acidity 6. Example output: (alpha centauri, 12).

title: Vampire Clan Blood Bank
spec: Write a SQL function `inventory(volume)` that evaluates blood stock levels across hidden vampire sanctuaries. The database includes a sanctuaries table with the identifier, region name, and elder in charge, and a donations table with the sanctuary identifier, blood type, and liters collected. Match the sanctuaries and donations to calculate the total liters collected per region. Exclude donations of animal blood types. Group by region name and blood type, and return the region name, blood type, and total liters for groups where the total liters fall below the given volume parameter. Order alphabetically by region name. Example input: volume 50. Example output: (transylvania, o negative, 30).

title: Mermaid Pearl Harvesting
spec: Create a SQL function `appraise(luster)` that identifies the most valuable oyster beds. A table of oyster beds has the identifier, ocean trench, and depth, and a table of harvested pearls contains the bed identifier, pearl color, and luster rating. Join the tables to find the average luster rating for each ocean trench. Only consider pearls with colors of black or gold. Group by the ocean trench and depth, and return the trench, depth, and average luster rating for beds whose average luster is strictly greater than the luster parameter. Sort the final output by average luster descending. Example input: luster 8. Example output: (mariana, 10000, 9.2).

title: Time Police Temporal Violations
spec: Implement a SQL function `penalize(severity)` that aggregates temporal law infractions by rogue chrononauts. A chrononauts table holds the identifier, alias, and origin era, while an infractions table logs the chrononaut identifier, violation type, and severity score. Link the tables to calculate the sum of severity scores for each alias. Filter out minor violation types like uniform code or loitering. Group the records by alias and origin era, keeping only those whose total severity score is larger than the severity parameter. Output the alias, origin era, and total severity score, ordering the results by total severity from highest to lowest. Example input: severity 50. Example output: (chronos, twenty first century, 150).

title: Zombie Apocalypse Safe Zones
spec: Write a SQL procedure `fortify(capacity)` that finds overcrowded survival outposts. There is a table of outposts with their identifier, base name, and maximum population, and a table of survivors containing the outpost identifier, survivor name, and age. Join the outposts and survivors tables to count the total number of survivors in each base. Only count survivors whose age is greater than twelve. Group by base name and maximum population, and select outposts where the total survivor count exceeds both the maximum population and the capacity parameter. Return the base name and the total survivor count, sorting alphabetically by base name. Example input: capacity 100. Example output: (fortress alpha, 150).

title: Robot Factory Assembly Defects
spec: Create a SQL function `inspect(faults)` that identifies production lines with high defect rates in android manufacturing. A production lines table contains the identifier, factory floor, and supervisor, and a quality checks table records the line identifier, batch number, and number of defects found. Join the tables to calculate the average number of defects per factory floor. Exclude batches manufactured during the night shift. Group the data by factory floor and supervisor, and return the factory floor, supervisor, and average defects for groups where the average exceeds the faults parameter. Sort the output by average defects descending. Example input: faults 5. Example output: (sector seven, smith, 8.5).

title: Magical Beast Containment
spec: Write a SQL procedure `secure(breaches)` that flags wildlife preserves failing to contain dangerous creatures. A preserves table contains the identifier, region, and warden name, and a breach log table records the preserve identifier, creature type, and severity level. Join the tables to count the total number of breaches per warden. Ignore breaches involving harmless creatures like pixies or fairies. Group by the region and warden name, and return the region, warden name, and total breaches for wardens who have a total breach count higher than the breaches parameter. Order the results by total breaches descending. Example input: breaches 3. Example output: (black forest, hagrid, 7).

title: Interdimensional Portal Routing
spec: Create a SQL function `optimize(latency)` that identifies slow transit routes between parallel universes. A portals table holds the identifier, dimension name, and energy source, and a transit logs table contains the portal identifier, traveler count, and transit delay. Combine the tables to find the maximum transit delay for each dimension name. Exclude transit logs where the traveler count is less than ten. Group the records by dimension name and energy source, and filter for groups where the maximum transit delay is greater than the latency parameter. Return the dimension name, energy source, and maximum delay, sorted by delay descending. Example input: latency 500. Example output: (dimension x, dark matter, 850).

title: Leprechaun Rainbow Gold Tracking
spec: Implement a SQL procedure `hoarders(coins)` that finds leprechauns hoarding excessive amounts of gold. A leprechauns table stores the identifier, clan name, and hat color, while a pots of gold table records the leprechaun identifier, location, and coin count. Link the tables to calculate the total coin count for each leprechaun clan. Exclude pots of gold located in fake or illusionary rainbows. Group by the clan name and hat color, and return the clan name, hat color, and total coin count for clans whose total coin count is greater than the coins parameter. Sort the output from highest to lowest total coin count. Example input: coins 5000. Example output: (shamrock, green, 15000).

title: Gondola Oar Carving Analysis
spec: Implement a function `analyze(connection)` that runs a database query to evaluate oar production. The database has a table of artisans with their identifier, workshop region, and certification status. A second table tracks carved oars, containing the artisan identifier, wood type, carving hours, and inspection grade. Join the tables to find the average inspection grade for each workshop region. Filter the data to only include artisans with a master certification status and where the carving hours are greater than forty. Group the results by workshop region. Order the final list by the average grade in descending order. Name the calculated average as average grade. Return a list of tuples with the region and average grade. For example, given an artisan in Venice who is a master, and an oar taking forty five hours with a grade of nine, the output is [("Venice", 9)].

title: Lute Rosette Carving
spec: Create a function `evaluate(database)` that queries lute instrument manufacturing records. One table holds lute models with an identifier, body style, and current production status. A related table logs rosette carvings with the model identifier, pattern complexity, carving duration, and acoustic resonance score. Connect these tables to determine the highest acoustic resonance score per body style. Restrict the evaluation to models in an active production status and where the carving duration is less than twenty hours. Create an alias for the maximum score called peak resonance. Combine the records by body style and arrange the output alphabetically by body style. Output a list of tuples containing the style and peak resonance. Example input with a renaissance style active model taking fifteen hours and scoring eight yields [("renaissance", 8)].

title: Kaleidoscope Mirror Alignment
spec: Write a procedure `report(database)` to extract data about kaleidoscope manufacturing. The first table lists mirror batches with an identifier, glass tint, and supplier quality flag. The second table records assembly tests, storing the batch identifier, prism angle, reflection bounces, and visual clarity rating. Merge the data to calculate the total visual clarity rating for each glass tint. Only process records where the supplier quality flag is approved and the reflection bounces are greater than twelve. Label the sum as total clarity. Group the outcome by glass tint and sort from highest to lowest total clarity. Return a list of pairs with the tint and total clarity. If an approved batch of blue glass has fifteen bounces and a clarity of seven, the result is [("blue", 7)].

title: Snow Globe Water Clarity
spec: Design a function `summarize(connection)` to run a query on snow globe testing data. A table of globe designs contains an identifier, winter scene theme, and sealing method. A second table logs clarity tests, including the design identifier, weeks aged, glitter density, and water cloudiness index. Join these sources to find the average water cloudiness index for each winter scene theme. Limit the analysis to designs using a vacuum sealing method and where the weeks aged is greater than ten. Assign the name average cloudiness to the result column. Aggregate the rows by winter scene theme and order by the average cloudiness from lowest to highest. Return tuples of the theme and average cloudiness. Example: a vacuum sealed cabin theme aged twelve weeks with a cloudiness of two returns [("cabin", 2)].

title: Abacus Bead Sliding Friction
spec: Provide a function `measure(database)` that analyzes abacus usability. A materials table stores an identifier, bead wood type, and rod coating material. A friction tests table contains the material identifier, humidity level, sliding force applied, and travel distance. Link the tables to compute the average travel distance for each bead wood type. Filter the records to include only beeswax rod coating material and where the humidity level is less than fifty percent. Rename the calculated average as mean distance. Group by the bead wood type and sort the output by mean distance in descending order. The function should return a list of tuples with the wood type and mean distance. A mahogany bead on beeswax at forty humidity traveling ten units results in [("mahogany", 10)].

title: Wind Chime Tube Resonance
spec: Construct a function `analyze(database)` to query wind chime acoustic properties. An inventory table holds an identifier, metal alloy name, and weather resistance rating. A sound testing table tracks the inventory identifier, strike force, sustain duration, and harmonic richness score. Join the tables to find the maximum sustain duration for each metal alloy name. Exclude any records unless the weather resistance rating is premium and the harmonic richness score exceeds eighty. Label the maximum duration as longest sustain. Group the information by metal alloy name and order alphabetically by the alloy name. Output a list of tuples containing the alloy and longest sustain. For a premium bronze chime scoring eighty five with a ten second sustain, return [("bronze", 10)].

title: Hourglass Sand Flow Calibration
spec: Develop a function `calibrate(connection)` to retrieve hourglass performance metrics. The first table details hourglass frames with an identifier, glass shape, and structural integrity pass. The second table logs sand flow trials, noting the frame identifier, sand grain size, ambient temperature, and flow duration variance. Connect the tables to calculate the minimum flow duration variance for each glass shape. Only consider rows where the structural integrity pass is true and the ambient temperature is strictly twenty degrees. Call the aggregate column lowest variance. Group the findings by glass shape and sort by the lowest variance ascending. Return a list of tuples of glass shape and lowest variance. Given a true passing bulb shape at twenty degrees with a variance of three, the output is [("bulb", 3)].

title: Feather Quill Ink Retention
spec: Implement a function `process(database)` that runs a query on calligraphy quill testing. A quills table has an identifier, bird species origin, and curing chemical used. A writing tests table includes the quill identifier, ink viscosity, pressure applied, and total words written. Join both tables to compute the average total words written per bird species origin. Filter out data to only keep records where the curing chemical used is alum and the pressure applied is classified as light. Assign the name average capacity to the calculated average. Group the data by bird species origin and sort by average capacity descending. Return tuples of the species and average capacity. An alum cured goose quill used with light pressure writing fifty words produces [("goose", 50)].

title: Wax Seal Stamp Engraving
spec: Write a function `review(connection)` to extract stamp manufacturing statistics. A stamp models table contains an identifier, handle material, and engraving style. A stamping trials table holds the model identifier, wax temperature, release time, and impression crispness score. Merge the tables to determine the average impression crispness score for each engraving style. Restrict the query to models with a brass handle material and where the wax temperature is over ninety degrees. Alias the average as average crispness. Group the results by engraving style and order them by average crispness from highest to lowest. Output a list of tuples with the style and average crispness. A brass handled floral style stamped at ninety five degrees scoring nine gives [("floral", 9)].

title: Tapestry Loom Thread Tension
spec: Create a function `evaluate(database)` to query loom weaving errors. A threads table provides an identifier, dye color, and fiber composition. A weaving sessions table tracks the thread identifier, loom tension setting, weaving speed, and warp snap count. Link the tables to calculate the total warp snap count for each fiber composition. Include only the rows where the dye color is indigo and the loom tension setting is high. Name the summed column total snaps. Group the records by fiber composition and sort the output by total snaps in ascending order. The function must return tuples of the fiber composition and total snaps. An indigo wool thread woven at high tension snapping twice returns [("wool", 2)].

title: Cigar Box Guitar Intonation
spec: Formulate a function `report(connection)` that runs an SQL query on instrument building data. A guitars table lists an identifier, box brand, and neck wood type. A tuning tests table contains the guitar identifier, string gauge, bridge height, and fret intonation accuracy. Join the tables to find the average fret intonation accuracy for each neck wood type. Filter the query to only evaluate guitars where the box brand is vintage and the bridge height is exactly low. Label the average as mean accuracy. Group the data by neck wood type and arrange the list by mean accuracy descending. Return a list of pairs showing the wood type and mean accuracy. A vintage brand guitar with a maple neck and low bridge scoring ninety eight yields [("maple", 98)].

title: Didgeridoo Beeswax Mouthpiece
spec: Provide a function `summarize(database)` to analyze didgeridoo player feedback. An instruments table has an identifier, timber type, and bore diameter. A feedback table records the instrument identifier, beeswax temperature during application, playtime duration, and player comfort rating. Join these tables to calculate the maximum player comfort rating for each timber type. Filter the records to those where the bore diameter is wide and the playtime duration is greater than sixty minutes. Name the maximum rating as peak comfort. Aggregate the results by timber type and sort alphabetically by timber type. Return a list of tuples containing the timber and peak comfort. A wide bore eucalyptus instrument played for seventy minutes with a comfort of eight returns [("eucalyptus", 8)].

title: Theremin Antenna Capacitance
spec: Develop a function `analyze(connection)` to retrieve electronic instrument metrics. A theremins table stores an identifier, circuit design version, and casing material. A calibration table tracks the theremin identifier, antenna length, room humidity, and pitch bend range. Merge the tables to compute the average pitch bend range for each circuit design version. Ensure you only include theremins with a walnut casing material and where the room humidity is below forty percent. Alias the computed average as average range. Group the output by circuit design version and order by average range from highest to lowest. Output tuples of the circuit version and average range. A walnut cased version two theremin at thirty humidity with a range of five gives [("version two", 5)].

title: Croquet Mallet Head Density
spec: Implement a function `measure(database)` that executes a query on croquet equipment. A mallets table includes an identifier, head wood type, and handle grip texture. A swing tests table logs the mallet identifier, swing velocity, impact force, and ball travel distance. Join the tables to determine the average ball travel distance for each head wood type. Limit the evaluation to mallets with a ribbed handle grip texture and where the impact force is greater than two hundred. Call the average column mean distance. Group by head wood type and sort the results by mean distance in descending order. Return a list of tuples containing the wood type and mean distance. A ribbed grip ash wood mallet hit with two hundred ten force traveling thirty meters produces [("ash", 30)].

title: Oboe Reed Scraping Symmetry
spec: Write a function `evaluate(connection)` to summarize reed crafting quality. A reeds table holds an identifier, cane origin region, and scrape profile style. A vibration tests table includes the reed identifier, breath pressure, humidity, and vibration balance score. Connect the tables to find the minimum vibration balance score for each cane origin region. Keep only the rows where the scrape profile style is traditional and the breath pressure is strictly high. Assign the alias lowest balance to the minimum score. Group the data by cane origin region and arrange by lowest balance ascending. The output should be a list of tuples of the region and lowest balance. A traditional scraped French cane tested at high pressure scoring seven returns [("French", 7)].

title: Papier Mache Mask Rigidity
spec: Create a function `process(database)` to query theater mask durability. A masks table contains an identifier, character archetype, and paper base type. A stress tests table records the mask identifier, drying days, applied weight, and structural deformation percentage. Join the tables to calculate the average structural deformation percentage for each paper base type. Filter the results to only include the hero character archetype and where the drying days exceed five. Name the result average deformation. Combine the records by paper base type and sort by average deformation from lowest to highest. Output tuples of the paper type and average deformation. A hero mask made of newsprint dried for six days deforming ten percent gives [("newsprint", 10)].

title: Sleigh Bell Harness Tone
spec: Construct a function `report(connection)` to extract acoustic data for sleigh bells. A harnesses table lists an identifier, strap leather type, and buckle metal. A ringing tests table tracks the harness identifier, horse trotting speed, ambient snow depth, and jingle decibel peak. Merge the tables to compute the maximum jingle decibel peak for each strap leather type. Exclude any records unless the buckle metal is brass and the horse trotting speed is greater than fifteen. Label the maximum value as maximum decibels. Group the findings by strap leather type and order them alphabetically by the leather type. Return a list of pairs of the leather type and maximum decibels. A brass buckled harness with a bridle leather strap at twenty speed hitting ninety decibels yields [("bridle", 90)].

title: Tuning Fork Vibration Decay
spec: Design a function `summarize(database)` to analyze acoustic laboratory tests. A forks table holds an identifier, target musical note, and steel alloy grade. A decay tests table logs the fork identifier, strike mallet material, overtone interference, and pure sustain duration. Join the tables to calculate the average pure sustain duration for each target musical note. Only process rows where the steel alloy grade is medical and the overtone interference is less than five. Create an alias for the average called average sustain. Group the output by target musical note and sort by average sustain descending. title: Agave plant pina harvesting
spec: Provide `analyze(fields, pinas)` to assess mezcal ingredient yields. The fields table includes the identifier and altitude, while the pinas table records the field identifier, sugar content, and weight. Filter for agave hearts with a sugar content exceeding twenty four brix from fields located at high altitudes. Connect the tables using the field identifier to calculate the average weight of the harvested hearts per field. Group the output by field identifier and sort the average weights in ascending order.

title: Cacao pod roasting profiles
spec: Formulate a SQL module `profile(roasters, batches)` to standardize chocolate making. You are given a roaster table with the identifier and drum type, and a batch table showing the roaster identifier, roast duration, and bitterness score. Select batches roasted for exactly forty minutes that resulted in a low bitterness score. Join the tables via the roaster identifier to sum the total number of optimal batches per drum type. Show the drum type and the batch count, grouped by drum type and ordered descending by the count.

title: Coffee cherry wet processing
spec: Develop `process(stations, cherries)` to evaluate coffee bean washing. The stations table provides the identifier and water source, while the cherries table lists the station identifier, defect rate, and total mass. Filter the records for a spring water source and a defect rate below two percent. Merge the tables on the station identifier to compute the total mass of high quality cherries processed by each station. Output the station name and total mass, sorting the results alphabetically by the station name.

title: Tea leaf withering durations
spec: Design a SQL script `review(racks, leaves)` to optimize oolong tea preparation. The database features a racks table with the identifier and airflow setting, and a leaves table containing the rack identifier, moisture loss, and resting hours. Identify leaves that rested between eight and twelve hours on racks with high airflow. Link the tables using the rack identifier to find the average moisture loss per rack. Group by the rack identifier and return it alongside the average loss, sorted by the loss from lowest to highest.

title: Yerba mate gourd curing
spec: Construct `inspect(artisans, gourds)` to check traditional vessel quality. You receive an artisans table with their identifier and workshop city, and a gourds table detailing the artisan identifier, curing days, and finish quality. Keep only the gourds cured for more than five days that achieved a smooth finish. Combine the tables on the artisan identifier to count how many premium gourds each workshop city produced. Output the city and the gourd count, ordering the list from highest to lowest count.

title: Sea salt evaporation ponds
spec: Write a query in `yield(basins, harvests)` to track artisanal salt collection. The basins table includes the identifier and salinity level, while the harvests table holds the basin identifier, crystal size, and collected mass. Restrict the data to coarse crystal sizes originating from basins with very high salinity. Join the tables using the basin identifier to calculate the total collected mass for each basin. Group the results by basin identifier and order them by total mass in descending sequence.

title: Himalayan pink salt mining
spec: Create `extract(tunnels, blocks)` to assess mineral block extraction using SQL. There is a tunnel table with the identifier and depth, and a block table showing the tunnel identifier, pink hue intensity, and weight. Filter for blocks with a vibrant hue intensity extracted from tunnels deeper than two hundred meters. Match the tables via the tunnel identifier to determine the maximum block weight found in each tunnel. Return the tunnel identifier and maximum weight, sorting by weight from largest to smallest.

title: Charcoal kiln burning times
spec: Implement `monitor(kilns, burns)` to oversee wood carbonization. The kilns table contains the identifier and brick type, alongside a burns table listing the kiln identifier, sustained temperature, and ash percentage. Select burn records where the temperature exceeded five hundred degrees and the ash percentage was below five. Connect the tables on the kiln identifier to find the average ash percentage for each brick type. Output the brick type and average ash, grouped by brick type and ordered ascending by ash percentage.

title: Peat bog cutting yields
spec: Provide a database function `summarize(tracts, cuts)` to analyze traditional fuel harvesting. The tracts table offers the identifier and moisture rating, while the cuts table records the tract identifier, slice thickness, and volume. Filter the cuts for a thickness of exactly ten centimeters from tracts rated with moderate moisture. Join the tables using the tract identifier to sum the total volume harvested per tract. Show the tract identifier and total volume, grouping the data and ordering by volume descending.

title: Thatch roof reed harvesting
spec: Formulate a SQL script `calculate(marshes, bundles)` to assess roofing material quality. You are given a marshes table with the identifier and water level, and a bundles table showing the marsh identifier, stalk length, and flexibility score. Isolate the bundles with a stalk length over one meter and a high flexibility score. Merge the tables on the marsh identifier to count the number of premium bundles harvested per marsh. Output the marsh location and bundle count, sorted alphabetically by location.

title: Ostrich egg incubation
spec: Develop `hatch(incubators, eggs)` to track poultry breeding success. The incubators table details the identifier and humidity setting, while the eggs table lists the incubator identifier, shell thickness, and hatch time. Filter for eggs with thick shells that hatched in under forty days. Link the tables using the incubator identifier to compute the average hatch time for each humidity setting. Group the results by the humidity setting and order them from quickest to slowest average hatch time.

title: Macadamia nut cracking
